issues.description: The problem statement and UML use the abstract method name messageOnFeed() for Animal, but elsewhere in the problem text (and the song specification) it refers to getFeedingSound(). This inconsistent method naming will confuse students about which method to implement and which method to call in Farm.singFarmSong() and feedAllAnimals(). The solution and template use/expect messageOnFeed(), but the problem description instructs usage of getFeedingSound() in key places (feeding and song), creating a mismatch between spec text and intended implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Standardize the method name across the problem statement, template, and solution. Either: (a) Update the problem statement (and UML/song description) to consistently reference messageOnFeed(), or (b) rename the abstract Animal method in template/solution to getFeedingSound() and update all calls accordingly. Ensure all examples (feedAllAnimals, singFarmSong) and test descriptions use the same method name.

issues.description: The concept of an animal feeding sound is referenced with two different method names: messageOnFeed() (used in the UML and implemented in the solution) and getFeedingSound() (mentioned in task descriptions). This inconsistency appears within the problem description and instructional comments and will confuse students about which method to implement and call (leading to mismatches against the reference implementation/tests).
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the method name for the feeding sound across all artifacts. Prefer using messageOnFeed() (as in the UML and solution) and update all occurrences of getFeedingSound() in the problem statement and template instructions to messageOnFeed(). Alternatively, if getFeedingSound() is preferred, rename the abstract method and all implementations to getFeedingSound() and update tests accordingly so all artifacts use the same identifier.
